history.summary: UNCERTAIN IDENTITY / THIN SOURCING. Kaleshwar Mahadev is the Shiva shrine on the EAST side of the Maa Chinnamastika temple campus at Rajrappa — one of four Rudra Mahadev guardian temples (East-Kaleshwar, West-Narahna, North-Muchhkund, South-Shiv Bari) whose presence gives the shrine its 'Dham' status (see seq 1641). No independent web sources document this shrine's founding date, patron or history beyond this guardian role; it should not be confused with the Kaleshwar Mahadev temples of Kangra (Himachal Pradesh) or Kaleshwaram (Telangana). Related to seq 1641 (Chinnamasta Temple, same campus) — complementary record, not a duplicate. Coordinates approximate (Rajrappa Project area). Specific image of the Kaleshwar shrine unavailable after genuine searching; media shows the Rajrappa temple complex.

name: Kaleshwar Mahadev Temple, Rajrappa
town_description: Rajrappa is a pilgrim town in Chitarpur block of Ramgarh district, at the confluence of the Damodar and Bhairavi rivers. It is famous as the seat of the Chinnamastika Shakti Peeth, drawing thousands of pilgrims daily, and also hosts the Rajrappa coal mining project. The town has guesthouses, dharamshalas and local transport links from Ramgarh and Ranchi.
